# OrbitBurn API (Space Monkeys)

> REST API for a burning activity calendar built from NASA FIRMS satellite fire hotspots (MODIS and VIIRS harmonized into one consistent record), a real-time fire map fused from NOAA GOES-East and NASA FIRMS, and a 7-day fire forecast. JSON over HTTPS, GET only except one POST, no authentication.

Base URL: `https://orbitburn.discloud.app` (local development: `http://localhost:8000`). Interactive docs: `/docs`. Full contract (OpenAPI 3.1, the source of truth): `docs/api/openapi.yaml` in the repository https://github.com/ryangustav/Space-Monkeys. This file is also served at `/llms.txt`.

Read these rules before calling the API:

- Units differ by route family and must never be mixed. `/history/*` counts **fire cell-days**: one 0.1° grid cell (about 11 km) on one UTC day with at least one detection. It is not a count of hotspots, not fire intensity and not burned area. `/forecast` gives a **probability** of at least one VIIRS fire detection per 0.25° cell (about 27 km) per day. `/fires/*` and `/detections/*` are individual fires and detections.
- `/history` is observational (what happened). `/forecast` is a model prediction for the next 7 days. Do not present one as the other.
- Dates are ISO 8601 UTC days (`YYYY-MM-DD`); periods include both `start` and `end`. Coordinates are WGS84 degrees; a bounding box is `bbox=west,south,east,north`.
- `null` means "no data from that sensor for that period" (before it started or after it ended). `0` means "observed, no fire".
- The historical record covers Brazil (biomes from IBGE 2019); the live map and forecast cover Brazil plus a margin.

## History: burning activity calendar

Every `/history` route except `/history/meta` and `POST /history/areas` needs exactly one area parameter:

- `bbox=west,south,east,north`, or
- `biome=` one of `Amazon`, `Caatinga`, `Cerrado`, `Atlantic Forest`, `Pampa`, `Pantanal`, or
- `area_id=` returned by `POST /history/areas` (kept in server memory; lost on restart, then the route answers 404 and the polygon must be registered again).

A cell belongs to the area when its centre is inside. Every response repeats the area as `area: {kind, cells, bbox|biome|area_id}`.

Series (`series=` parameter): `harmonized` (default; the one to show), `modis` (observed MODIS fire cell-days, integers, 2000-11-01 on) or `viirs` (observed fire cell-days of any VIIRS satellite, 2012-01-20 on). `viirs` is **not comparable across years** (new satellites in 2018 and 2023 add detections), so climatology, anomaly, season and trend reject it with 422. A harmonized value is MODIS-equivalent: the MODIS count while MODIS delivers data, and afterwards an expected count estimated from VIIRS, given as `{value, low, high}` (90% interval) with `harmonized_source` `modis`, `viirs_estimate` or `mixed`. Buckets with `provisional: true` come from near-real-time files not yet in the FIRMS standard archive.

Two more series split VIIRS into layers instead of rescaling it: `viirs_only` (expected fire cell-days the VIIRS satellite saw that MODIS would not have: small fires) and `detected` (VIIRS estimate + `viirs_only`: expected cell-days with fire seen by MODIS or that satellite). Both count one satellite at a time, so they are comparable across years from the first complete year of the layer (2013); they are null before 2012, where no sensor saw small fires. Use `harmonized` for the long record since 2000 and `detected` for how much fire is detectable now. `GET /history/meta` → `harmonization.layers.check` scores `detected` against what MODIS or the satellite actually saw on the reference years.

- `GET /history/meta`: what the record covers. Call once on start. Returns `coverage` per sensor and satellite (`start`, `standard_until`, `end`), `biomes` with cell counts, `harmonization` (`status` `available` or `pending`, `switch_date`, `model`, `test_metrics`), `known_gaps` (sensor, period, note) and `limits` (`max_area_cells` 50000, `max_map_cells` 20000, `max_day_buckets` 1000).
- `POST /history/areas`: register a drawn polygon. Body `{"geometry": <GeoJSON Polygon or MultiPolygon>}`. Returns `{area_id, cells, bbox, biomes}` where `biomes` is the share of cells per biome (`outside` for cells outside Brazil).
- `GET /history/calendar?start=&end=&granularity=week` + area: fire cell-days over time. `granularity` `day`, `week` (default) or `month`. Returns `buckets: [{start, end, harmonized: {value, low, high}, harmonized_source, modis, viirs, viirs_only, detected, provisional}]`. Weeks are days 1–7, 8–14, … of the year; week index 51 runs to 31 December.
- `GET /history/climatology?series=harmonized&granularity=week` + area: the normal year. Optional `base_start_year`, `base_end_year` (default base starts in 2003 and ends at the last complete year). Returns `base_years` and `buckets: [{index, label, median, p10, p90, mean}]` (index = week 0–51 or month 1–12).
- `GET /history/anomaly?start=&end=&series=harmonized` + area: is this period (at most one year) above normal? Returns `value`, `normal: {median, p10, p90}`, `percentile` (share of base years with a lower value, %), `ratio_to_median`, `class` (`below` < p10, `normal`, `above` > p90, `record`), `base_years`, `excluded_years`.
- `GET /history/season?year=&series=harmonized` + area: when the fire season started, peaked and ended. Returns `total`, `start_week`, `peak_week`, `end_week` (first day of each week), `normal: {start, peak, end}` as `MM-DD`, and `complete_year` (false for the current year: dates may still move).
- `GET /history/trend?series=harmonized` + area, optional `start_year`, `end_year`: yearly totals and the long-term trend. Returns `annual: [{year, value, interval, complete}]`, `slope_per_year` (fire cell-days per year), `ci95`, `significant`, `method: "theil-sen"`.
- `GET /history/map?start=&end=` + area: fire cell-days per 0.1° cell in a period. Returns `cells: [{cell_id, lat, lon, harmonized, modis, viirs}]` (only cells with fire).

Errors: 400 area missing or ambiguous, 404 unknown `area_id`, 409 harmonized series not available yet (use `series=modis`), 413 area or response too large (see `limits`), 422 invalid input (message says why), 503 historical data not loaded on this server. Error body: `{"detail": "..."}`.

## Forecast: next 7 days

- `GET /forecast?min_p=0.05&bbox=w,s,e,n`: probability of at least one VIIRS fire detection per 0.25° cell for each of the next 7 days. Lead 1 is today. Returns `issued_for` (last day of observed data), `valid_dates` (7 dates), `generated_at`, `anchored_at`, `resolution_deg`, `model`, and `cells: [{lat, lon, p: [7 probabilities], anchored}]`, only cells whose highest probability reaches `min_p`. `anchored: true` means a fire burning now (seen by GOES or FIRMS in the last hours) raised that cell above the model's own forecast. 503 until the first forecast is issued (it needs the server's FIRMS key).
- `GET /forecast/outlook?bbox=w,s,e,n` or `?biome=Pantanal`: the forecast summed over an area, next to the normal for the same dates. Returns `days: [{date, expected_fire_cells, normal_fire_cells, ratio_to_normal}]` and `week` totals. `ratio_to_normal` above 1 means more fire expected than usual. Units are forecast cells (0.25°, VIIRS), not the fire cell-days of `/history`: never add or compare the two. `biome` works only when the server has the historical data.
- `GET /forecast/model`: model card. Data used, inputs, test scores on Brazil 2024–2025 (`test_avg_precision`, `test_brier`, compared with climatology and persistence) and `status`.

The model is a U-Net trained on the NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP archive (2012–2022); since S-NPP ended (2026-11-02) it is fed with VIIRS NOAA-20 near-real-time detections. On the 2024–2025 test it reached average precision 0.396 versus 0.303 for climatology. It forecasts fires that keep burning much better than new ignitions. Present its output as a probability, never as certainty.

## Live: real-time fires

- `GET /fires/live?bbox=w,s,e,n&min_confidence=0`: fire events of the last 48 hours as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, each event fused from detections of several satellites (GOES-East ABI every 10 min, VIIRS, MODIS). Properties: `fire_id`, `uncertainty_km` (about 95% radius), `confidence` (0–1, a heuristic score for ranking, not a probability), `sensors`, `n_detections`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `frp_max_mw`. Plus `updated_at`.
- `GET /detections/recent?bbox=&sensor=VIIRS|MODIS|ABI&limit=5000`: raw detections (GeoJSON), newest first.
- `GET /fires/stream`: Server-Sent Events. One `snapshot` event (same body as `/fires/live`) on connect, then a `pulse` event after every poll (about every 10 min: `at`, `new_detections`, `total_fires`, `new` and `updated` as GeoJSON, `removed` as fire ids) and a `forecast` event when the forecast is re-anchored (`issued_for`, `anchored_at`, `anchored_cells`). Comment lines `: ping` keep the connection open.

## System

- `GET /health`: `{"status": "ok"}`.
- `GET /status`: real-time worker state, last success or error per data source, live totals and number of stream subscribers.

## Example questions and the call that answers them

- "How did the 2020 fire season in the Pantanal compare with normal?" → `GET /history/anomaly?biome=Pantanal&start=2020-07-01&end=2020-10-31`, then `GET /history/season?biome=Pantanal&year=2020`.
- "Is fire activity in the Cerrado rising over the years?" → `GET /history/trend?biome=Cerrado`.
- "Which weeks are usually critical around Brasília?" → `GET /history/climatology?bbox=-48.5,-16.2,-47.3,-15.4`.
- "Where is it burning right now in Mato Grosso?" → `GET /fires/live?bbox=-61.6,-18.1,-50.2,-7.3`.
- "Where is fire likely in the next days near Porto Velho?" → `GET /forecast?bbox=-64.5,-9.5,-63.0,-8.0&min_p=0.2`.

## Data sources

NASA FIRMS (MODIS Collection 6.1 and VIIRS 375 m active fires), NOAA GOES-R ABI Fire/Hot Spot Characterization (GOES-19, via NOAA Open Data on AWS) and IBGE biome boundaries (2019). Full citations and licenses are in the repository README.
